Benchmark survey for Stage 1 evaluation. Closest existing benchmark: AgentSimulator (Kirchdorfer et al. 2024, arXiv 2408.08571): 9 public logs (Loan Application, P2P 608 cases, CVS, Confidential 1000/2000, ACR, Production, BPI12W, BPI17W), temporal 80/20 case split excluding cases spanning the split, 10 simulation runs, metrics NGD/AED/CED/RED/CTD from log-distance-measures (already installed), published numbers for Simod, DGEN, DSIM, AgentSim. Its P2P log is not our data/benchmark P2P (1000 cases), and its repo ships only LoanApp raw data; other logs need locating (Zenodo 5734443 cited by Ozdemir et al. 2025). Our earlier numbers are not comparable to published ones: different log, split, run count, and our Simod run was one-shot defaults. Blumel et al. 2026 (Process Science) list five validity threats: concept drift, fading phases in extraction, fading phases at split, data leakage, warm-up/cool-down. No public benchmark found for what-if accuracy. No runs executed.

Checked both Optimos repos for a Stage 2 benchmark. Original Optimos (roptimus-prime, 754a65c): 10 experiments shipped as model.bpmn + timetable.json + constraints.json under test_assets/experiments; one CLI command; installed in an isolated Python 3.11 venv and ran HC-FLEX 5 iterations on purchasing_example in 27 s (about 3.5 s per candidate, 3 simulations of 550 cases). Needs lock-file pins (prosimos 1.2.4, pix-framework 0.8.9, Prosimos fork c50f39e); unpinned install fails on 'exponnorm'. Ships no baseline results (output_files holds placeholders). Optimos v2 (8e0bfe5): baseline result stores live on the Tartu HPC cluster, not in the repo; each of 180 jobs is a SLURM script asking 10 h, 24 CPUs, 64 GB, up to 10,000 solutions; Python 3.10, forked Prosimos, torch. Both score a set of cost/time trade-offs against the joint front of all contestants (hyperarea ratio, Hausdorff, purity, delta), not a single recommendation. Permitted moves are adding/removing resources and changing working hours within constraints; task-duration changes, used in all four Stage 2 runs, are not permitted moves. Not yet done: scoring an externally supplied timetable through their evaluator; checking the paper's iteration budget.

Spike: original Optimos scores a timetable it did not generate. A 25-line script builds RosterManager + PoolInfo from an external timetable.json, checks each resource with verify_masks (per day; the no-argument form only checks the first day) and verify_global_constraints, then calls perform_simulations. On loan_sc_lu: shipped start valid, cost 22791 / cycle time 33094 s; one shift removed valid, 24692 / 60221 s; everyone 24/7 rejected for all 20 resources; 5.6 s for the three. Findings: (1) only 6 of 10 shipped starting timetables pass Optimos's own checks (bpi2012, bpi2017, loan_mc_hu, loan_mc_lu, loan_sc_hu, loan_sc_lu); consulta, financial and purchasing_example start with never-work violations, production with global-limit violations. (2) Cost is (resource count + 1) x simulated duration in hours: Resource.cost_per_hour is fixed at 1 and hours worked are not counted. (3) A calendar whose id is absent from constraints.json is dropped silently, so the grader must compare counts. Spike script kept in the session scratchpad, not in the repo.

Second benchmark search before committing to a Stage 2 suite. No benchmark exists that scores an LLM agent on simulation-based process improvement. Closest LLM work: Lashkevich et al. 2024 (redesign prompts, judged by analyst interviews, no grader); Reis et al. 2026 and PM-LLM-Benchmark (process mining question answering, LLM-as-judge); SimBank 2025 (per-case interventions on one synthetic loan process, a different problem). New lead: orlenyslp/bpm-r-opt (5d52577, 2021), the predecessor of roptimus-prime. 8 processes, HC-STRICT/HC-FLEX/TS-STRICT/NSGA-II, and it ships the published results: every explored allocation with cost and cycle time per process and algorithm (e.g. 1252 allocations for BPI 2012, 3084 for purchasing_example; budget in bpropt.py is 10000 evaluations, 0.08 non-optimal ratio, 15 simulations per allocation). The only permitted move is headcount per resource pool, which is the move AutoTwin's compare_scenario already supports. Stage 1 BPI 2019 pass limits, fixed before any new run (user delegated the numbers: 'you decide the numbers... make sure its validated enough, if its not we try on a different data'). A model passes only if, on the held-out test period (5 seeds, mean): (1) every simulated case ends, zero loop-limit warnings; (2) simulated median and mean case duration each within +-25% of real; (3) simulated cases started per week within +-20% of real; (4) trigram distance <= 0.25; (5) seed-to-seed SD <= 10% of the mean for (2) and (3). Real and simulated cases are filtered by the same rule (start and finish inside the window) so window truncation hits both equally. Selection on validation (3 seeds), test touched once. Budget: at most 5 candidate revisions per data slice; if none passes, report no acceptable model and move to different data. Basis: accepted p2p_heuristics_v1 had mean cycle-time ratio ~1.22 and path distance 0.0418; +-25% and 0.25 are my judgement, not published standards.
